Low-Cost Second Passports in 2026: São Tomé vs. Nauru

Both nations offer a legal route to citizenship through qualifying investments. Neither requires physical residence as a condition of applying.

So which one is better?

What Is the Better Second Passport?

The low-cost second passport refers to the lowest-cost citizenship-by-investment program available to qualifying foreign nationals. Cost includes the minimum qualifying investment, government fees, due diligence fees, and authorised agent fees.

São Tomé is an affordable option for investors. But Nauru remains a lower-cost alternative. Both have different minimum investment thresholds, and processing timelines also vary, depending on the program.

The suitable program depends on what you need from a second citizenship.

São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment

São Tomé is a small island nation in the Gulf of Guinea, off the West African coast. São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment program has lower minimum investment requirements. Applicants do not need to reside in São Tomé before or after applying. Dual citizenship is also allowed if your application is approved.

How Does São Tomé Citizenship Work?

Qualifying investors can invest in the country’s National Transformation Fund. An authorised agent like North Arista processes applications, which include government due diligence, document submission, and investment fulfilment after approval.

Step 1: Choosing an investment route

São Tomé’s program has only one qualifying route for applicants. The minimum investment is US$90,000 for a single applicant. This is subject to program requirements and government and processing fees.

Step 2: Preliminary due diligence

At the start, your authorised agent conducts an assessment. The outcome of this decides if you meet the program’s character, financial, and background requirements. If you clear the initial test, your agent then submits your application.

Step 3: Document preparation

You submit your documents to your agent. Documents must be certified and submitted in the prescribed format. You are required to submit accurate documents. Any disinformation may cause a disqualification.

 Step 4: Government review

The São Tomé government reviews your application. They have their own due diligence process. This review determines the future of your application. In case of not meeting the set criteria, your application may be rejected.

Step 5: Fulfil the investment

When you clear the government review, you’re asked to complete the qualifying investment within the given timeframe. The timeframe depends on the investment route you choose.

Step 6: Receive your passport

Once your citizenship by investment application is approved, you receive your certificate and apply for a São Tomé and Príncipe passport. São Tomé allows dual citizenship.

São Tomé Passport Visa-Free Access

The São Tomé passport lists 90+ destinations as visa-free or visa-on-arrival. This access depends on each country’s entry rules and regulations.

Europe

You need a visa to visit Schengen member states. The countries include France, Germany, Portugal, Spain, Italy, etc.

United Kingdom

São Tomé and Príncipe citizens need a UK visa for visits and transit, subject to UK immigration rules and regulations.

Africa

Regional African destinations are accessible if you have a São Tomé passport. This depends on bilateral agreements and entry rules of the country you’re visiting.

Nauru Citizenship by Investment

Nauru, officially the Republic of Naoero, is an island republic in the Pacific Ocean. Its citizenship-by-investment program targets qualifying foreign nationals. Qualifying investors can invest in a government-approved project. Physical residence is not a condition to fulfil. Dual citizenship is allowed.

How to Get Nauru Citizenship

The program offers one nauru citizenship by investment route: a non-refundable contribution to a government-approved project. You can submit applications through an agent. The process involves background checks, document review, and government due diligence.

Step 1: Choose your investment route

Nauru’s standard contribution is US$115,000, but a limited-time US$25,000 discount currently reduces the contribution to US$90,000 for applications filed before 31 December 2026. Additional fees apply for application filing, due diligence, and passport issuance.

Step 2: Preliminary due diligence

Your agent conducts an initial background review. This identifies any eligibility issues before you submit the application. The outcome of this review matters.

Step 3: Document preparation

Your agent provides you with a list of required documents. You must submit all documents in English and certified. This stage typically takes up to 30 days.

Step 4: Submit the application

The authorised agent submits the formal application. Government authorities conduct their own due diligence and review your application. This requires an interview for every principal applicant, either virtually or in person, and due diligence applies to applicants aged 16 or above.

Step 5: Fulfil the investment

After the approval of your application, you’re required to complete your investment in a given timeframe. Your agent will confirm payment instructions.

Step 6: Receive your passport

Upon approval, you receive your Certificate of Naturalisation. You may then apply for a Nauru passport, which will be issued and delivered through the prescribed channel.

Nauru Passport Visa-Free Access

The Nauru passport provides visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 110+ destinations. Your access depends on each country’s entry rules and other requirements.

Europe

Nauru citizens need a Schengen visa for short stays. This applies to all states, including France, Germany, Portugal, Spain, and Italy. Short-stay access does not allow the right to work in any member state.

United Kingdom

You must have a visa to visit the UK. There’s no agreement between the two countries for visa-free or visa-on-arrival access.

Pacific and Commonwealth Nations

Regional Pacific destinations and select Commonwealth nations are accessible under certain entry conditions. Your entry is subject to each destination’s rules.

São Tomé vs. Nauru: How the Programs Compare

Both programs are legal citizenship-by-investment options for qualifying investors. Neither program requires physical residency for its citizenship. Both allow a dual citizenship option. You can also include eligible family members, subject to each program’s requirements and eligibility criteria.

Investment

São Tomé’s minimum investment is US$90,000 for a single applicant. Nauru’s standard contribution is US$115,000. A discounted rate of US$90,000 under Nauru’s Iruwa Initiative is available until 31 December 2026. The base contribution applies outside that period. You must verify current total costs through an authorised agent.

Processing

São Tomé’s approval takes about 2-3 months after you submit a complete, verifiable application. Actual processing can vary depending on how long each stage takes. Passport issuance may take longer than approval itself.

Nauru’s process takes three to four months for approval. Investment fulfillment and passport issuance are the subsequent steps. Both timelines depend on the completeness of your documentation, your background, and government review.

Visa Access

Neither passport currently provides visa-free access to the Schengen Area. Both require a visa for short stays across Schengen member states. Neither provides visa-free entry to the United Kingdom.

Nauru’s passport covers 110+ destinations on a visa-free or visa-on-arrival basis. São Tomé’s covers approximately 90+ destinations. Both figures are indicative and subject to change if government policy changes.

Requirements

Both programs have similar eligibility criteria, subject to each program’s current regulations.

You must be at least 18 years old. You must meet each program’s character, security, and due diligence requirements. You must meet applicable health requirements. Your investment funds must come from a legal and verifiable source.

Required documents include a valid passport from your country of origin, a certified birth certificate, a police clearance certificate, medical documentation where required, bank statements supporting your source of funds, passport-size photographs, proof of address, and a marriage certificate or equivalent where applicable.

Submit all documents in the prescribed format and ensure they are appropriately certified. Requirements vary by program and individual applicant circumstances.

Is Either a Good Second Passport?

That depends on what you need.

If European mobility is a priority, neither passport currently provides visa-free access to the Schengen area. Both require a visa for short stays to Schengen destinations. Europe is not a mobility advantage for either program.

If the investment amount is the primary factor, both programs are currently advertised at US$90,000, although Nauru’s amount is presented as a limited-time offer.

Neither passport provides a direct route to the United States. If US market access matters to you, a Caribbean CBI program may be more relevant.

Both programs allow eligible dependants to be included in the same application, subject to each program’s applicable dependency and eligibility criteria.

Final Thoughts

São Tomé and Nauru are two legal options for a second passport. For cost-conscious investors, both São Tomé and Nauru currently offer a US$90,000 investment option. Nauru’s rate is a limited-time offer valid until 31 December 2026.

Neither program provides visa-free access to the Schengen Area or the UK. Neither provides a route into the US market. Both permit dual citizenship. Both allow eligible family members to be included. Neither requires physical residence before or after applying.

What each program offers is defined. What it does not offer is equally defined. For qualifying investors for whom cost is the primary factor, São Tomé and Príncipe is worth serious consideration.

An authorised agent can confirm current investment minimums, total fee structures, processing timelines, visa access, and eligibility requirements before you commit to either program.
